描述_EN: the simple stylised lines on the monk’s robe underline the sparse and spiritual aesthetic of the figure as a whole. cast iron came into use for outdoor sculpture during the song dynasty (960–1279) because of a bronze shortage. after casting, the surface was covered with gesso, lacquer, paper and paint. these have since disappeared, to reveal the coarse casting lines that show how the figure was made in sections and then welded together.
描述_ZN: 僧侣长袍上简单的风格化线条强调了整个人物的稀疏和精神美学。 宋代（960-1279）时，由于青铜器的短缺，铸铁开始被用于室外雕塑。 在铸造之后，表面被涂上石膏、漆、纸和颜料。 这些东西后来都消失了，露出了粗大的铸造线，显示了这个人物是如何被分段制作然后焊接在一起的。
